meta.title: Vision-Language Models
meta.thesis: Vision-Language Models is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A claims assistant reads receipt images and answers questions with visual evidence. By the end, they should be able to build or review VLM input-output contract with image, question, evidence, and uncertainty fields, measure visual claims grounded in visible regions, and catch the failure where the model invents text that is not present in the image.

mentalMap.title: Vision-Language Models: mental map
mentalMap.caption: Use VLMs by aligning image and text inputs, asking visual questions, checking grounding, and routing uncertain outputs to verification.
mentalMap.oneLineThesis: Vision-language models connect visual evidence to language, but their answers still need grounding, OCR, and task-specific checks.

blocks.title: The model sees an encoded image plus your question

spans.text: Problem anchor: a learner uploads a screenshot of a broken lesson editor and asks what is wrong. A vision-language model takes an image and a text prompt, then outputs text. It may describe UI elements, answer visual questions, read some text, or reason over diagrams, depending on model and prompt.

blocks.analogy: A VLM is a language model with a visual notebook beside the prompt.

spans.text: Prompt: "Describe the visible error state. Cite the exact UI region you used. Do not guess hidden settings." Good answer: "The publish button is disabled; the visible warning above it says citations missing." Weak answer: "Your database is broken," which is not visible evidence.

modules.title: The prompt defines the visual task
modules.sub: Captioning, OCR, diagram reasoning, and UI debugging need different asks.
modules.summary: VLM prompting should specify evidence, uncertainty, and output structure.
objectives: Ask for evidence rather than guesses.

blocks.title: Do not ask one vague question of every image

spans.text: "What is in this image?" invites a broad caption. A debugging prompt should ask for visible UI state, exact readable text, likely user-facing issue, and uncertainty. A diagram prompt should ask for nodes, arrows, labels, and ambiguities.

modules.title: Grounding failures hide inside fluent answers
modules.sub: VLMs can misread text, counts, spatial relations, and causality.
modules.summary: Verification should target the visual facts the model used.
objectives: Use evidence requests and manual checks.
Avoid high-impact automation from raw visual answers.

spans.text: VLMs can hallucinate UI elements, misread small text, count objects incorrectly, or infer causes not visible in the image. Ask for evidence: visible text, approximate region, uncertain fields, and what cannot be determined from the image alone.

A VLM says an arrow points from Retrieval to Answer, but the diagram arrow actually points from Retriever to Reranker. The answer sounded plausible because those concepts are related. Verification catches the visual relation.

modules.title: Code an image-text inference call
modules.sub: A minimal run should preserve image source and review status.
modules.summary: Use a VLM pipeline with prompts, but keep verification metadata.

blocks.title: Image-text-to-text inference pattern
blocks.code:
from transformers import pipeline

pipe = pipeline("image-text-to-text", model="HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-Instruct")
messages = [{
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
        {"type": "image", "url": "lesson-editor-error.png"},
        {"type": "text", "text": "Describe the visible error. Quote exact text if readable and say what is uncertain."},
    ],
}]
result = pipe(text=messages, max_new_tokens=120)
print(result)

spans.text: Model names and APIs can vary; the durable idea is to ask a task-specific visual question and preserve image source plus review status.

predictThenReveal.prompt: Why ask the model to say what is uncertain?
predictThenReveal.answer: It discourages unsupported guesses and gives reviewers a list of fields that need human or tool verification.

spans.text: Checklist: image source logged; prompt asks for evidence and uncertainty; output structured if downstream code uses it; OCR/counts verified; high-impact actions gated by review.

modules.title: VLM answers need provenance and tool backup
modules.sub: Use OCR, detection, or humans when exact visual facts matter.
modules.summary: The release gate depends on stakes and verifiability.
objectives: Decide when VLM output is enough.

blocks.title: Use the VLM as a reasoner, not final authority for exact pixels

spans.text: For low-risk tutoring summaries, a VLM answer with evidence may be enough. For exact UI text, counts, legal or medical content, or actions in tools, pair it with OCR, detectors, structured UI state, or human review. Keep the original image linked so corrections are possible.

blocks.ruleOfThumb: Let VLMs explain visual context; verify exact text, counts, identity, and actions with stronger evidence.
blocks.useWhen: Use VLMs for screenshot help, diagram explanation, image-grounded tutoring, and visual search triage.
blocks.avoidWhen: Avoid treating raw VLM answers as proof for high-impact decisions or exact OCR without verification.

blocks.title: VLM gate
blocks.prompt: A VLM reads a tiny warning label in a screenshot. What should you do before using it in a support answer?

options.text: Assume the fluent answer is exact.
Verify the text with OCR, zoom, UI state, or human review.
